summary: Frontend-only verification of the 'leads never open / Server is busy' fix in LeadDetail.jsx. Verified via Playwright network interception that opening a lead is now decoupled from the 5 secondary GETs — the page renders as soon as /api/leads/{id} succeeds, even if messages/activities/whatsapp/calls/attachments/followups all fail with 504. All 6 planned scenarios PASS.

integration_issues.issue: During resilience test (all secondary endpoints 504), React dev-mode overlay 'Uncaught runtime errors: Request failed with status code 504' briefly appeared over the (correctly rendered) lead-detail-page. Root cause: not all secondary API calls in LeadDetail.jsx have a .catch() — FollowUpSection.load() at ~line 1081 does `API.get(/leads/{id}/followups).then(...)` with no .catch, so its 504 becomes an unhandled promise rejection. Same likely applies to other child components (WaLeadPanel handles it; audit AuditLog / CallerActivities). This is dev-mode only (no user-visible overlay in production build) but is untidy and clutters the console.

Proves core GET is no longer gated on Promise.all of secondaries.

action_items: OPTIONAL POLISH (non-blocking): Add .catch(() => {}) to remaining secondary fetches inside LeadDetail sub-components (FollowUpSection.load at line ~1081, CallerActivities load, AuditLog load) so they don't surface as unhandled promise rejections in the React dev overlay when the backend is degraded. User-facing behavior in production build is already correct.
critical_code_review_comments: LeadDetail.load() fix is correct and minimal: `await API.get('/leads/'+id)` first, setLead(l), then fire the 5 secondary GETs independently each with .then/.catch. Render guard `if (!lead) return <Spinner/>` at line 231 is correct.

Note: child components (FollowUpSection, CallerActivities, AuditLog, WaLeadPanel) also do their own fetches on mount; most of these still lack .catch, so under sustained backend degradation they will produce unhandled rejections. Consider applying the same fault-tolerant pattern in those components.
context_for_next_testing_agent: iter71 verified the LeadDetail Promise.all → sequential-core-then-fire-and-forget refactor via Playwright route interception. Method: page.route('**/api/**', ...) fulfills 504 for the 5 secondary endpoints while leaving /api/leads/{id} untouched. Assertion: [data-testid="lead-detail-page"] AND [data-testid="lead-name"] render within 15s, AND [data-testid="assignee-select"] visible = Assignment card rendered from core lead only. Negative check for CORE 504 confirms spinner+no-crash. Any follow-up should focus on adding .catch handlers to child-component fetches to eliminate dev-overlay noise.
rca of the issue: USER REPORT: 'LEADS DONT OPEN — server is busy... leads never load.' RCA (root-caused by main agent, verified here): LeadDetail.load() previously did `await Promise.all([GET /leads/{id}, GET /messages, GET /activities, GET /whatsapp/lead/{id}, GET /calls/lead/{id}, GET /attachments])`. Because Promise.all rejects on the first failure, a single slow/504 secondary GET on the loaded production DB rejected the whole promise, so `lead` state was never set → `if (!lead) return <Spinner/>` kept the page on an infinite spinner and apiErr() showed the hardcoded 'Server is busy right now — please try again in a moment.' toast. FIX: split load() into (1) `await API.get('/leads/'+id); setLead(l)` and (2) fire the 5 secondary GETs independently as `.then(...).catch(() => {})` so their failure never blocks the core lead from rendering. VERIFIED: with all 5 secondaries returning 504 via Playwright route interception, both test leads (500210, 600027) open and show core data + Assignment card. Before the fix this would have hung forever.
